cookerModels.name: Instant Pot 6-Qt / 8-Qt (Duo / Pro / Ultra)
cookerModels.reliefValveType: Weighted Steam Release Handle with Silicone Float Pin
cookerModels.interlockType: Mechanical Pin Lock with Microswitch Sensor
cookerModels.canningWarning: Electric multi-cookers lack thermal feedback calibration for elevation and fluctuate pressure between heating cycles. USDA / NCHFP guidelines explicitly prohibit using electric multi-cookers for low-acid canning due to lethal Clostridium botulinum spore survival risk.

cookerModels.name: Crock-Pot Express & Ninja Foodi Multi-Cookers
cookerModels.interlockType: Bayonet Lid Rotation Catch with Lock Pin
cookerModels.canningWarning: Not USDA certified for low-acid canning. History of CPSC recall (Crock-Pot Recall #21-035) where lids could detach before full depressurization if forced.

cookerModels.name: Stovetop Modern Spring-Valve Cooker (Kuhn Rikon, Fagor, WMF)
cookerModels.reliefValveType: Spring-Loaded Pressure Indicator Valve & Rim Escape Cutout
cookerModels.interlockType: Pressure-Activated Handle Pin & Locking Rim Lugs
cookerModels.canningWarning: Cooks at true 15 PSI (250°F), but standard pots lack the thermal mass and jar capacity required by USDA canning protocols. Use only for high-acid boiling-water style processing if container approved.

cookerModels.name: Vintage Weighted-Jiggle Cooker (Presto, Mirro Aluminum)
cookerModels.reliefValveType: Free-Floating Counterweight on Vent Pipe (5/10/15 PSI)
cookerModels.interlockType: Visual Interlock Pin or Cam-Lock Handle
cookerModels.canningWarning: Lacks calibrated dial gauge; overpressure rubber plug can dry out, degrade, or blow under rapid thermal cycling.

cookerModels.name: Dedicated Stovetop Pressure Canner (All American 921 / Presto 23-Qt)
cookerModels.interlockType: Clamping Positive Screw Wing Nuts or Heavy Locking Cam
cookerModels.canningWarning: Meets USDA / NCHFP thermal death time (TDT) standards for home canning of vegetables, soups, seafood, and red meat when operated at validated PSI.

foodTypes.name: Split Peas, Lentils & Dried Legumes
foodTypes.recommendedRelease: Natural Pressure Release (NPR) strictly required (minimum 20 min). Quick release will suction thick foam into vent pipe.
foodTypes.warning: Split peas generate proteinaceous foam that coats the anti-block shield and welds the float valve shut, creating an unvented pressure trap.

foodTypes.name: Oatmeal, Porridge, Quinoa & Barley
foodTypes.warning: Starch gelatinization creates viscous bubbly lather capable of clogging the steam release aperture.

foodTypes.name: Whole Dried Beans (Black Beans, Chickpeas)
foodTypes.warning: Never fill over 1/2 line. Add 1 tbsp cooking oil to break surface tension and minimize foaming.

foodTypes.name: Applesauce, Cranberries, Polenta & Purees
foodTypes.recommendedRelease: Full NPR only. Never quick release.
foodTypes.warning: Thick purees splatter violently and erupt when atmospheric pressure drops suddenly.

foodTypes.name: Bone Broth, Stocks & High-Liquid Soups
foodTypes.warning: High thermal mass retains heat; quick release causes superheated broth to geyser out of the vent pipe.

foodTypes.name: Meat Roasts, Poultry & Stew Meat
foodTypes.recommendedRelease: 10-15 Minute NPR to keep meat juicy and prevent boiling-out.
foodTypes.warning: Safe standard profile; ensure minimum 1 cup (250 ml) thin water liquid is present to generate steam.

foodTypes.name: Low-Acid Canning (Green Beans, Meat, Stocks)
foodTypes.recommendedRelease: Slow Natural Cooling to 0 PSI; sudden depressurization vents jar seals and causes siphoning.
foodTypes.warning: Clostridium botulinum neurotoxin thrives in anaerobic low-acid canned food (pH > 4.6). Requires sustained 240°F–250°F (115°C–121°C) at verified 10–15 PSI.

fillLevels.label: 2/3 Full (Max Safe Line for Normal Foods)
